answer: Before a hull is built, the master shipwright lays its keel and writes the ship's name, the timber's mark and the day in the keel register. A walnut hull claimed as laid fails the register: the keel must rest on the stocks at the karst of the yard, and a hull never laid has no keel to show. Forging a false laying means bribing the shipwright, faking forty entries and paying 13,400, while the zenith page in the register is read at every launching, so a hull whose keel was never laid is left on the stocks.
